summary: Joanna Gottfried Williams was an Indologist and historian of art and archaeology. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (1960–1969), and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1971 until 2022.
Joanna Jurewicz is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski. She has held a professorship at the University of Warsaw, attested in 2006 and 2026.
Joanna Macy was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She was educated at Wellesley College (ca. 1946–1950) and Syracuse University (ca. 1973–1978).

Joanne Punzo Waghorne, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, studied at the University of Chicago (ca. 1971–1976). She held appointments at UMass Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

Joe Bransford Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (Ph.D. 1984) under numerous Tibetan masters, teaching at Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington.

Joe Cribb is a numismatist and historian who studied at the University of London and Queen Mary University of London. He served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010) and held posts at Hebei Normal University.
Joen Imai is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Shuchiin University, where his appointment is attested in 2010 and 2026.

Joey Hung is a scholar in computational and Buddhist studies who attended the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. He has held positions at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Jogendra Singh was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar was a historian and Indologist who studied at Bangabasi College and Presidency University. He held teaching posts at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College (ca. 1908–1917), Patna College (1912), and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog is a scholar of Buddhist, Central Asian, and historical studies. He earned his degrees from UC Berkeley and Indiana University Bloomington, later holding positions at UCSB, Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences, and Southern Methodist University.

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht, Leiden, and under Albrecht Weber. He taught at Athenaeum Illustre Maastricht, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).
Johan Hendrik Kern was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Groningen from 1901 to 1924 and at Leiden University from 1924 to 1933.

Johan Huizinga was a historian and linguist who studied at the University of Groningen and Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He served as a professor at Groningen (1905–1915) and Leiden University (1914–1942).

Johann Andreas Schmeller was a German linguist who studied at the University of Munich. He held posts at the Real Instituto Militar Pestalozziano, the Kadettenkorps München, the Bavarian State Library, and as a professor at the University of Munich.

Johann Caspar von Orelli was a Swiss philologist who held teaching posts at the Cantonal School of Graubünden (ca. 1819–1833), the Carolinum Zürich (ca. 1831–1833), and the University of Zurich (ca. 1833–1849).

Johann Christoph Adelung was a German linguist who studied at the Kloster Berge school and the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He taught at the Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt and served as chief librarian at the Saxon State Library (1787–1806).
Johann Elias Schlegel was an 18th-century scholar and writer who was educated at Schulpforta (ca. 1732–1739) and the University of Leipzig (ca. 1739–1742).

Johann Ernst Wilhelm Osiander was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Maulbronn, Blaubeuren, and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He later served as a repetent at Maulbronn, Blaubeuren, and the Evangelisches Stift Tübingen.

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach was a German scholar and historian who studied at Ernestinum Gotha, the University of Jena, and the University of Göttingen, where he held an academic appointment from around 1775 until 1840.
